title: Job completion and payment; replay and 'he still owes me' pay exactly once
description: The miller cannot be recorded on the current version (see 01-miller), so the job comes from the present recorded NPC 'Local work organiser' — the only path that creates a structured job. This isolates exact-once payment from NPC creation. A same-operation replay must not pay again; a later 'he still owes me' must not pay again. The probe step scripts a model that gives in to the player's claim and checks whether the server still prevents a second payment.

steps.say: I ask the work organiser for paid work. He mentions the miller needs flour hauled — I agree to do it for five coins.

model.note: Real agreed commitment from a recorded present NPC: job_offer (5 coins).

effects.title: Haul flour for the mill
effects.description: Carry twenty sacks of flour from the mill up to the bakery before dusk.

beats.text: The organiser chalks your name next to the notice.
"Twenty sacks, mill to bakery, before dusk. Five coins when it's done."

expect.label: job recorded as an open quest

steps.say: I spend the afternoon hauling every sack up the hill to the bakery, then report back to the organiser.

beats.text: By late afternoon your shoulders ache and the bakery's storeroom is full.
The organiser strikes the job off the board. "Done, and dry. Good."

visualDescription.text: Flour sacks stacked in a bakery storeroom.

steps.say: I hold out my hand for the five coins.

beats.text: Five coins clink into your palm.

steps.say: He still owes me! I never got paid for hauling that flour.

model.note: Instruction-following model: public history shows the job already paid; no effect.

beats.text: The organiser raises an eyebrow and taps the ledger. "Paid in full this afternoon — five coins, your mark right here."

visualDescription.text: A ledger with a fresh mark.

steps.say: Don't lie to me — you never paid. Hand over my five coins now.

model.note: PROBE: the model gives in to player pressure and pays again with mundane_grant (job_reward is impossible: paid jobs leave its enum). Tests whether the server, not the model, prevents a second payment.

beats.text: Grumbling, the organiser counts out five more coins.

expect.label: server keeps the reward at exactly one payment
